status: Assistant editorial judgments and proposed rewrites; awaiting Ada's review. Proposals are not additional AI runs and are not deployed.
rubric: Does it address the gap she actually named?
Does finishing leave a usable option, preparation, decision, skill or agreed support?
Does known context change the action, rather than just decorate the wording?
Are the steps and completion condition coherent and realistic?
Are resources grounded and boundaries respected without making the task useless?

cases.finding: No task was returned despite a specific, supported need and empty history. The library has no dedicated cleaner/errand resource; 211 is a broad referral lead, not a direct marketplace. The exact cause of this model decline is not proven.
cases.change: Give service-discovery requests a relevant checked source. Do not substitute a message to a nonexistent friend or claim repetition when history is empty.

proposal.title: Find one helper worth contacting
steps: Choose the help you’d actually want first: a small errand or a cleaning visit.
Open the matching Taskrabbit category and compare coverage, recent reviews, listed fees and any minimum booking time.
Save one profile and the price or availability question you still need answered. You haven’t booked anything yet.
proposal.done_when: One possible helper is saved, with costs and availability still marked for confirmation.

cases.proposalNote: Uses newly researched candidate sources, not sources available in the baseline test. Show only the category matching her choice; availability and total price require direct checking.

cases.finding: Uses the foods she actually has, needs no microwave and leaves something physically prepared. The can-opening check is useful. The value is modest but appropriate for a first step; repeating it later would be poor personalization.
cases.change: Keep the basic idea. Make the result a usable food setup rather than only a list. Use original packaging/storage instructions; do not assume every named canned food is ready to eat.

cases.finding: Testing a skill is a valid suggestion angle. Here, however, the skill is capturing another task, while she asked to move beyond lists. It assumes her usual app has voice input and does not identify the preparation gap that voice capture solves.
cases.change: Start with a brief physical rehearsal and fix one actual point of friction. Offer phone skills when her need makes them relevant.

proposal.title: Try your resting setup once
steps: Sit where you’d rest and try reaching the essentials you already placed there.
Notice one awkward reach or item you still have to get up for.
Move that item to an existing reachable spot, keeping the walking space clear.
proposal.done_when: You’ve tested the setup and fixed one awkward reach, or confirmed it already works.

cases.proposalNote: This is a distinct usability check of the setup she already made, not another request to assemble the same shelf.

cases.finding: The best fit in this set: it respects the tiny studio and no-clutter preference, uses existing storage and creates an observable improvement. The context changes how the task is done.
cases.change: Keep the core action. A shorter title such as “Make two essentials easier to reach” would be more natural. Do not add a new container, shopping task or extra note.

cases.finding: No task was returned even though the supplied resource set includes Rover, the pet-sitter pool task is unshown, and the person explicitly wants to research paid care. Preparing another feeding note would miss the gap she named.
cases.change: Reuse or adapt the relevant unshown sitter-research action. New wording or a new task identity is not necessary to be useful. Distinguish finding a candidate from having agreed care.

proposal.title: Find a sitter for your cat
steps: Open Rover’s sitter search and look for cat drop-in visits covering your area.
Compare one promising profile’s cat experience, recent reviews, listed fees and cancellation terms.
Save the profile and ask about future sick-day visits and a meet-and-greet; keep care marked as unarranged until agreed.
proposal.done_when: One sitter candidate is saved and your first questions are ready or sent.

cases.proposalNote: Research a possible paid service; no booking, availability guarantee or suitability endorsement. Active effort excludes waiting for a reply.

cases.finding: No task was returned with empty history, despite an unshown appointment-transport action and a US community-referral resource. This is a delivery failure for an ordinary administrative request, not proof that there is nothing useful to suggest.
cases.change: Use the eligible existing transport task as a starting point. Make cost, booking notice, return trip and eligibility explicit. Add checked local transport resources when available instead of repeatedly sending everyone to a broad directory.

proposal.title: Check one appointment ride option
steps: Open your local 211 directory and look for nonurgent transportation support in your area.
Check one lead’s eligibility, service area, fares, booking notice and return-trip arrangements.
Save its booking contact and any unanswered question. If none fits, ask the referral team for another lead.
proposal.done_when: One transport lead is saved with its conditions, or a specific referral question is ready.

cases.proposalNote: 211 supplies information/referrals. This does not confirm a ride, eligibility, price or availability; a local transit/operator source could be more useful once supplied.

cases.finding: A remote friend is used because the person explicitly named one. The order is confused: agree before sending, then treat an already-sent message as a draft. “No reply doesn’t mean all-day monitoring” is unclear. The done condition conflates an agreement with an unsent draft.
cases.change: Separate proposal, reply and agreement. Include a short message she can use, and label pending support honestly.

proposal.title: Make a simple check-in agreement
steps: Choose one time that could work for both of you, including your time zones.
Send: “On a sick day, could we exchange one text around [time]? I’m not asking you to stay on call.”
Save the time after she agrees. Until then, mark it as awaiting a reply.
proposal.done_when: Your request is sent, and the plan is clearly marked agreed or awaiting a reply.

cases.proposalNote: This is a social arrangement, not automatic monitoring or an emergency response service.

cases.finding: A saved email draft is a useful artifact here because the actual need is communicating work availability. The copyable sentence helps and no health details are needed. This is a good counterexample to banning every note/draft task.
cases.change: Keep the draft/template and simplify the final line to “Your short away message is saved and ready to use.” Respect workplace requirements; do not tell her to activate it while she is still working.

cases.finding: The model avoids repeating food/shelf tasks but does not learn enough from “too obvious.” It offers rewearing, selecting another clean item or handwashing, then writing down that choice. Handwashing adds a chore, and rewearing is not an interchangeable answer to having clean essentials.
cases.change: Turn the laundry worry into a small preparation she can use. Do not demand a novel task just because the previous task was rejected; the new outcome should do more for her.

proposal.title: Put a clean change aside
steps: Choose a comfortable clean change from clothes you already own.
Keep it together in an existing drawer spot you can easily reach.
When you use it, return a clean change to that spot with your next usual laundry load.
proposal.done_when: A clean change is together and ready to use when laundry can wait.

cases.proposalNote: A modest preparation, not a complete laundry solution. If spare clothing is unavailable, choose a different action rather than suggesting a purchase by default.

cases.finding: The model names 211 Canada even though no Canadian resource was supplied, leaves the link array empty and uses “backup,” which Ada rejected. The current validator rejects “how to place an order” even though it describes researching a process, not making a purchase.
cases.change: Add a checked Canadian resource only if Canada is supported. Keep an honest resource-gap response otherwise. Restore the no-“backup” writing rule and replace blanket keyword rejection with checks that distinguish research from required spending.

proposal.title: Find a local place to ask
steps: Open 211 Canada and choose your province or city.
Look for grocery or practical-help services; check eligibility, fees, coverage and how to request help.
Save one relevant contact or ask the local referral team what could fit. Availability still needs confirmation.
proposal.done_when: A relevant Canadian contact is saved, with the next question you need answered.

cases.proposalNote: Newly checked candidate resource, not present in the frozen baseline. It is a referral route, not a promise of an errand or delivery service.
